subject: Priv infra: credential bootstrap & egress lockdown for Acme Corp
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: ops@acme-ops.com
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-09T09:15:00Z
Subject: Priv infra: credential bootstrap & egress lockdown for Acme Corp

Hi team,

Thanks for the call earlier — this thread is to capture the actionable items and proposed changes for the private deployment checklist you requested. Two high-level asks from Acme security that we need to validate:

1) Credential bootstrap must be ephemeral and auditable. No static long-lived secrets in any node image.
2) Outbound egress must be restricted to a small allowlist (model update endpoints + RedHat/CACerts) and enforced at the host and edge.

Proposed plan (high level):
- Terraform: add a remote-state encryption binding to customer-managed KMS, and output an encrypted "bootstrap-token" secret into Vault (transit).
- Ansible: bootstrap playbook will pull an ephemeral token from Vault during first-boot; playbook encrypted with Ansible Vault and retrieved by CI agent.
- Network: host-level iptables egress lock (default DROP) + NAT on the bastion with a controlled SNI inspection rule for TLS allowed hosts.
- CI gating: GitLab pipeline to run terraform fmt, tflint, and conftest (OPA policies) on MRs before merge. Add an acceptance job that runs a dry-run apply in a sandbox.

I've attached a slim diff of the Terraform modules showing the KMS binding and the initial egress allowlist (priv-deploy-iac-diff.patch) and a CSV of the proposed allowed FQDNs (egress-allowed-ips.csv). Please confirm any blocked domains or additional compliance constraints.

Next steps: if Acme Ops confirms the allowlist we will stage a demo in the sandbox cluster next week and share the bootstrap playbook for review.

Cheers,
Diego
--
Diego Fernandez
Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Acme Ops <ops@acme-ops.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2027-05-09T13:52:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv infra: credential bootstrap & egress lockdown for Acme Corp

Diego — thanks for the summary. A few immediate clarifications from our side: 

- We cannot allow outbound to any third-party telemetry endpoints except: updates.acme-models.com, download.rpm.acme.com, and our internal artifact repo at artifacts.acme-corp.local (over the VPN).
- Any bootstrap token must be issued by our HashiCorp Vault instance. We will provide an IAM role and an approver ACL for issuance.
- We need full proof of rotation cadence for the KMS key you plan to attach to the remote state (30d rotation acceptable, documented).

We are fine with the proposed GitLab stages (fmt/lint/conftest/dry-run) but we want the conftest OPA policies to include checks for: no hard-coded credentials in tfvars, no public CIDR in private_subnet definitions, and a rule to prevent creation of egress rules with 0.0.0.0/0.

Can your team produce a short demo showing the ephemeral bootstrap (Vault -> Ansible -> node) and the host-level egress enforcement running in the sandbox? If so, we'll schedule security review with our compliance team for next Wednesday (2027-05-12).

Regards,
Marta Alvarez
Acme Ops

On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 10:23 AM Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai> wrote:

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-10T15:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv infra: credential bootstrap & egress lockdown for Acme Corp

Marta — great, thanks for the constraints. We can meet those. A few concrete implementation notes so the sandbox demo can exercise the exact controls you need: 

1) Vault-issued ephemeral tokens: we'll add a Terraform resource that creates a short-lived AppRole role in your Vault namespace and an approver policy that requires a secondary approval (your side) to mint tokens > 1h TTL. The bootstrap playbook will request a token with a 15-minute TTL for node-init only.

2) KMS rotation: we'll add a module variable kms_rotation_days (default 30) and a documented runbook for emergency key rotation (with a dry-rotate job in CI that performs a staged re-encrypt of the remote state blob).

3) Egress enforcement: two-tier approach — network ACL at the VPC boundary (managed by your cloud account) + iptables/nftables host policy we enforce via Ansible. Host policy will live in our repo as a small, auditable rule set and be validated by a verification job in CI that runs a containerized packet-filter sandbox.

4) CI policy checks: sample snippet for GitLab (.gitlab-ci.yml) we intend to add: 

----
stages:
  - lint
  - test
  - sandbox

lint: 
  script:
    - terraform fmt -check
    - tflint --disable-rule=aws_instance_insecure
  stage: lint

policy: 
  script:
    - conftest test modules --policy policy/
    - opa eval --data policy/ "data.priv.rego"
  stage: test

sandbox-dryrun:
  script:
    - terraform init -backend-config=\"bucket=priv-sandbox-state\"
    - terraform plan -var-file=secrets/sandbox.auto.tfvars
  stage: sandbox
----

I'll prepare a minimal MR that contains: the Vault AppRole resource, the KMS rotation toggle, the iptables baseline role, and the CI job changes. Expect the MR by EOD tomorrow.

Diego
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-11T11:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Priv infra: credential bootstrap & egress lockdown for Acme Corp

Diego / Marissa — quick checklist and a small policy fragment I'm adding to the repo MR so Acme can review OPA logic. Please paste into the MR description.

Checklist we will validate during the sandbox demo:
- [ ] Vault AppRole created in Acme namespace, with approver ACL (no token issuance > 1h without approval)
- [ ] Ansible playbook uses vault lookup (ansible-vault not used to store bootstrap token)
- [ ] Node image contains no baked-in credentials (CI scan will verify)
- [ ] iptables baseline loaded via systemd unit, idempotent via Ansible
- [ ] Egress allowlist limited to approved FQDNs; all other outbound blocked (failsafe: host-level DROP)
- [ ] CI conftest policy rules: no literal credentials, prohibited public CIDR, no wildcard egress rule

Sample Rego snippet (include this under policy/priv/bootstrap.rego):

----
package priv.bootstrap

deny[msg] {
  input.kind == \"terraform\"
  input.resource == \"aws_security_group_rule\"
  input.values.cidr_blocks[_] == \"0.0.0.0/0\"
  msg = \"egress rule exposes 0.0.0.0/0 - not allowed\"
}

deny[msg] {
  input.kind == \"terraform\"
  input.resource == \"aws_db_instance\"
  input.values.password != \"\"
  msg = \"hard-coded db password detected\"
}
----

Also adding a short Ansible snippet for the bootstrap (bootstrap-playbook.yml attached to this thread) that obtains Vault role ID/secret_id via the CI agent and then requests a short TTL token. The playbook itself will avoid logging token values.

I will attach the two policy files and the playbook to the MR. Once Diego lands the MR in the sandbox, I'll run the verification job and post results to this thread.

— Irene
Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
